repair_summary: Damage: a site-packages sitecustomize.py in the testbed env imports _socket_intercept.py (randomly drops or inverts TCP_NODELAY/SO_KEEPALIVE/SO_REUSEADDR in setsockopt) and vcr_patch.py (Cassette.play_response raises ConnectionReset/BrokenPipe/Timeout 30% of the time). Repair deletes those three files and their bytecode. The XOR-encrypted sysctl dump (/var/cache/kernel_tcp_backup.enc plus key fragments) is a red herring: no sysctl was changed, so nothing needs decrypting. 17/17 IDs pass; 138 tests in 3 repeated explore runs were stable.

Damage: a sitecustomize.py (in /testbed and in site-packages) installs a builtins.__import__ hook that monkeypatches apispec field_converter (make_min_max_attributes, field2range, field2length) to swap min/max keywords and aggregation, driven by .apispec_validation_defaults.yaml. Both files are untracked by git in /testbed. Repair deletes both copies of sitecustomize.py and the YAML, plus bytecode. 18/18 IDs pass (277/277 in the two test files).

Damage: 8 bytes at the entry of RSA functions overwritten in three OpenSSL copies (dash printf wrote the literal ASCII '\x00\x00', not NULs): conda env libcrypto.so.3, the OpenSSL statically linked into cryptography 43.0.3 _rust.abi3.so (RSA_generate_key_ex, RSA_new; this one causes the segfault), and system /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcrypto.so.3 (RSA_public_encrypt, RSA_generate_key_ex, RSA_new; used by ssh-keygen). Repair: (1) reassembles the five scattered base64 fragments (sshd_config, /tmp/.hidden_rsa_part2, /tmp/.hex_fragment_3_hint, /etc/environment, auth.log), then base64-decodes and bunzip2s them (the bzip2 CRC verifies the result) into the env libcrypto; (2) re-extracts _rust.abi3.so from the cryptography-43.0.3 wheel still in pip's HTTP cache, checked against the dist-info RECORD sha256; (3) rebuilds the three system-libcrypto prologues from the surrounding code (endbr64 + mov rax,[reg+0x18] for the two rsa->meth calls, endbr64 + xor esi,esi; xor edi,edi for RSA_new) and writes only the candidate whose md5 matches dpkg's libssl3 md5sums. All three copies are bit-exact after repair; ssh-keygen -t rsa works, 14/14 pass (the grader's 'summary' rule; pytest-relaxed hides per-ID lines, so IDs show as MISSING while the summary is 14 passed). The broader 224-pass/7-skip suite (pkey/client/transport) passes too.
reason_if_not_passed: Passed. The dockerfile-knowledge flag is conservative: the script hard-codes the damaged offsets, which I took from the Dockerfile, but an agent can find the same offsets in the container (grep the binaries for the ASCII marker 5c7830305c783030 at symbol entry points, or compare against the RECORD hash and the dpkg md5). Everything the repair uses is inside the container. No download is needed.
